properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/27/2025 to MCCRACKEN OIL & GAS LLC in Foster Township, McKean county. 78.60(b)5 - DISCHARGE REQUIREMENTS - Owner or operator failed to spread tophole water or precipitation water from a pit over an undisturbed, vegetated area capable of absorbing the tophole water and filtering solids in the discharge, and spread in a manner that prevents a direct discharge to surface waters and complies with 25 Pa. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: MCCRACKEN OIL & GAS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/27/2025
Violation Code: 78.60(b)5 - DISCHARGE REQUIREMENTS - Owner or operator failed to spread tophole water or precipitation water from a pit over an undisturbed, vegetated area capable of absorbing the tophole water and filtering solids in the discharge, and spread in a manner that prevents a direct discharge to surface waters and complies with 25 Pa. Code Section 78.53.
Violation ID: 8223745
Permit API: 083-57711
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Foster Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/27/2025
Comments: This recently drilled conventional well was venting to the atmosphere at the time of inspection. The well permit and E and S plan are posted onsite. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. Drill cuttings from the well were directed into a lined pit on location. The road leading to the well has held up to recent drilling related traffic.At the time of the inspection, drill cuttings were observed in the snow at the northwest corner of the well pad. The cuttings were observed to continue into a nearby unnamed tributary (UNT) of Tunungwant Creek. Cutting residues and gray water were observed within the bed and banks of the stream channel. The operator reported that a large amount of tophole water was produced during the drilling process that could not be contained by the pit and needed to be pumped off location. The operator reported that the pH of the tophole water was 6.0 and conductivity was 240 micro Siemens per centimeter. Violations have been issued for failing to spread the tophole water over an undisturbed, vegetated area in a manner that prevents a direct discharge to surface waters. No corrective action is required and the violations are immediately closed.

Starting at approx. 09:00 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/21/2025 to KRIEBEL NATURAL GAS CO LLC in Manor Borough, Westmoreland county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: KRIEBEL NATURAL GAS CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/21/2025
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8226340
Permit API: 129-28077
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Manor Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/21/2025
Comments: On March 21, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release.At the time of the inspection the well site appeared unchanged from the Department's previous inspection on 3/20/2025.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. Other production equipment was observed on site and appeared to be charred, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. A production tank was observed on site with a large hole in its side, the tank had approximately 1-2 in of fluid pooled at the bottom of it, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this production tank.A soil conductivity reading was taken directly under the hole in the tank with a reading of 10.16mS. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. The Department observed 2 booms installed in the ditch. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of 10.43mS, 7.28mS, 1.27mS, 0.93mS, 0.68mS, 0.78mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. Conductivity readings were taken in this area of the ditch with readings of 0.53mS, 0.38mS, and 0.46mS.A conductivity reading was taken upstream of where the ditch appears to terminate with a reading of 0.67mS. A conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.76mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings obtained, it appears that the conductivity readings are comparable to the previous inspections in regards to distance and levels of elevated readings in the ditch. It appears that released fluids may have been contained to the portions of the ditch where standing fluid was observed, and it did not appear from the observations and readings that there was a release into Waters of the Commonwealth.Prior to leaving the site, the Department called operator representative Ben Dickun to inquire when remediation was going to begin. Mr. Dickun stated they have contacted their consultant (Moody) and that work to remediate as well as a site assessment/sampling by Moody was scheduled to occur on Tuesday, 3/25/2025. The Department recommended during the call that immediate measures are properly implemented to commence remediation in response to the brine release that occurred onsite during the 3/19/2025 incident to prevent further migration of the onsite pollution and prevent pollution into WOC.Based on today's inspection, violations issued during IR 3941481 and 3941519 shall remain outstanding.

Inspection Date: 2020-04-27
Comments: In an effort to prevent the spread of the COVID-19 virus, the Department has conducted this administrative inspection in response to information provided by Chief. Based on the analytical results for isotopic samples collected by Chief at the above-referenced well on 6/17/2019 and 11/15/2019, methane was detected as follows: 8.36 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 6/17/2019. 60.72 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. 94.78 % Methane detected at the Production (5 ½¿) x Intermediate (9 5/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. The presence of methane at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus is evidence of defective cement. Although the presence of methane was reported by the submittal of the associated isotopic data, defective cement was not corrected or a plan to correct the defect(s) was not submitted for the above-referenced well. As a result, a violation of 25 Pa. Code §78a.86 has been cited, which provides: ¿In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under § 78a.91 ¿ 78a.98 (related to plugging).¿ Therefore, please provide a written response within 30 days of receipt of this Notice of Violation, as to when and how the above-listed violations were or will be corrected, and what steps are being taken to prevent their recurrence.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/17/2025 to EQT PROD CO in Morris Township, Greene county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8249213
Permit API: 059-27655
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Morris Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/17/2025
Comments: On 09/17/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the Harden Farms Well Site following receipt of an incident report that was submitted to the Department on 09/17/2025 at 12:17 (CTS 392314).It was reported that 10 gallons of biocide material was spilled on site at 12:00, 09/17/2025. No waterways were affected. It was also reported that a clean up crew (SPSI) was on site.I called the EQT representative who reported the spill, Lance Witters, for information. I noted that SPSI arrived after I did, and I requested the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) to be sent to me. It was described to me that the material spilled was a Multi-Chem biocide. The cause of the release was that a hose back pressured, biocide flowed back to the tank, and the tank overflowed. It was estimated that 10 gallons spilled.SPSI had not began remediation and was not on the pad when I arrived. No personal were on the pad upon my arrival.The following was observed:The contaminated area was adjacent to the gas production units (GPUs). It was unknown if any production fluid was present in addition to the biocide spilled; no elevated conductivity was observed. No remediation had begun and SPSI was not on the pad when I arrived on the pad. SPSI arrived to the site after the Department (Photo 1). An extremely strong odor was experienced on site in the vicinity of the contaminated area.SPSI then arrived on the pad and had not begun remediation while I was on site. The impacted area was located between the well heads and the GPUs. The impacted area appeared wet with small sections of pooled fluid (Photos 2-5).I asked SPSI if they had the SDS, and they did not. The SDS was not located on site with the site documents in the mailboxes. I was able to locate a Control and Disposal Plan and the Site Specific Safety and Environmental Plan and Policy. I was not able to locate any information related to the Multi-Chem biocide (Photos 6-9). I also did not find a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC) on site. The SDSs are required to be on site. The PPC Plan is also required to be on site during drilling or completion activities, however the well operator shall prepare and develop a site specific PPC plan prior to storing, using, or generating regulated substances to, on or from a well site.The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance (Photo 10).The Department requests a description of the activities that were being carried out that resulted in a spill.Due to the SDS not present on site, a PPC Plan not on site, failure to control regulated fluids with a release to the ground, and failure to use secondary containment, violations of 78a.54, 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(i)5iD, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78a64a(b) are being issued.

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 913918
Permit API: 085-23966
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: Hempfield Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/14/2021
Comments: Stopped to investigate this complaint of oil overflowing a tank. Alan Wolf (DEP) was present. It was evident that the plastic brine tank had overflowed (no top lid and oil residue on top of tank and on the sides). There was oil saturated hay inside the diking. There was about 3 to 20 gallons of oil still in the diking. There was oil staining on the high ends of the inside of the diking indicating a significant fluid level that was once present and had dropped. The metal stock tank #64411, was about 1/4 full. The poly (brine) tank was also 1/4 full. There was stressed vegetation on the outside of the diking in roughly a 12' x 3' area. The conductivity was high in this area (20,000 micro siemens/cm with soil conductivity probe). The soil conductivity probe showed areas on average of 5,000 micro siemens/cm inside the diking about one foot deep. The gas well was producing with the annulus buried. The well was tagged. It had house gas plumbed off the 4" casing at the well with two regulators and a meter.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/16/2022 to PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC in Ridgway Twp, Elk county. 78a65(a)1i - SITE RESTORATION - Post Drilling - Owner or operator failed to restore the land surface within 9 months after completion of drilling all permitted wells on the well site or 9 months after the expiration of all existing well permits on the well site, whichever is later.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/16/2022
Violation Code: 78a65(a)1i - SITE RESTORATION - Post Drilling - Owner or operator failed to restore the land surface within 9 months after completion of drilling all permitted wells on the well site or 9 months after the expiration of all existing well permits on the well site, whichever is later.
Violation ID: 948140
Permit API: 047-24586
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Ridgway Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/16/2022
Comments: This unconventional well is currently equipped for production and is equipped with a well tag displaying the well’s API number. The site ID sign at the entrance of the pad includes the required information, however it has become faded. Drilling operations were completed on this well on 8/21/2011. There is a second active well (047-24580) on this pad for which drilling operations were completed on 7/20/2011. Pin Oak has failed to restore this well site according to approved plans associated with ESX11-047-0021 and more than nine months have passed since the completion of drilling the last permitted well on this well site. Approximately one-half of this pad does not appear to be actively used for the operation of this well. There are four steel tanks labeled as holding production water located inside of a lined steel containment on this well site. At this time, the containment appears sound, as it is holding several inches of stormwater. A well development impoundment (Impoundment # 5) is located approximately 900’ northeast of the HM1 well site. This impoundment is covered by the same ESCGP that encompasses the HM1 well site. The impoundment has not yet been restored, and greater than nine months have passed since the last well was serviced by this impoundment. The Department does not have record showing that this well development impoundment has been registered, as is required by Chapter 78a.59b(b). The water from this impoundment is currently being discharged via a 2" plastic pipe out of the southwest corner of the impoundment onto a vegetated swale. There are currently no surface concerns evident from this dewatering. The access road leading to this well site and well development impoundment is in general holding up to current traffic levels. Routine maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road to prevent potential E&S issues. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site & well development impoundment, as well as the access road banks appears to be established. Future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site & well development impoundment.

The washout created a "jetstream" of fluid with a reported ~9000 PSI of pressure behind it. This stream of fluid cut through the secondary containment liner, the primary containment liner, and dug through some pad material. An estimated 15 gallons of frack fluid and sand mixture was released through the hole. A vac truck was onsite to recover sand/fluid mixture from containment. Most of the fluid was recovered. The vac truck was also used to suck fluid that had collected in the hole through containment. While I was onsite, crew was flowing back and flushing the well to be able to shut it down. Kris plans to have the iron, rig mats, and containment pulled back to learn the extent of the void to fill it in for safety purposes. Upon soil screening of the area, impacted soils would be excavated and disposed of. Golder planned on taking soil samples from beneath the containment and the sampling results would be forwarded to the DEP. Due to findings throughout the course of this inspection, violations of the following are cited against well API #015-23420: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 35 P.S. 6018.301

Comments: This site located west off Greeley Road north of junction with Francis Road in a forested area. Tank battery, two brine tanks and one oil tank in secondary containment, located along the access road. Marshall Wurst found this tank battery with a lined secondary containment containing a release of 2-3 bbls of crude oil on 8/23/2019. WQS Taylor inspected this site on 8/28/2019 and issued an NOV to Coastal Petro Corp. for the release of crude oil into the lined secondary containment. Crude oil contamination is evident on the surface of the water and and on the outside of the tanks. An empty 200 gallon tote is set in the secondary containment between the oil tank and first brine tank. This well to be transferred from Coastal Petro Corp. to Titusville Oil & Gas Associates Inc., application for the transfer of wells was sent in on 11/18/2019. Titusville Oil & Gas Associates, Inc. is to complete the clean-up at this site.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Inspection Date: 10/31/2025
Comments: On 10/31/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 43 degrees, overcast and lightly sprinkling when I arrived on location. Rainfall has impacted the region in the last 24 hours.Upon my arrival, I first inspected the original south pad for the Taft 851 1V well. A plugged well monument is installed above the well with a plugged date of 3/24/2025. All servicing equipment has been removed from this pad. The pad has not been reclaimed and the temporary access road and temporary bridges remain installed.When I arrive on the active site, I met Seneca's Wes Sammins who described current operations as follows: Patterson drilling rig #805 has been mobilized to the site to drill an additional eight wells at the site. The rig was towered up over the 70HU, and had started drilling surface on 10/28/2025. The rig was currently drilling the intermediate at 1568 feet with the intermediate going to 3350 feet, then to total depth at 23514 feet. Wes expects to drill one more well that is in the process of being repermitted. Six wells have been completed this run. Secondary containment has been installed for drilling operations. 12 frac tanks, diesel tanks, and chemicals were staged in secondary containment around the drilling rig. Drill cuttings were being collected, solidified and temporarily stored in 6 dumpsters. 28 frac tanks remain staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. There are five newly drilled and completed wells on site that were staged for production. Sand separators were attached to the wells, the sand separators all connected to two frac tanks. Secondary containment remains installed around the wellheads. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs have been installed on site, all staged in secondary containment. Liquid in a 5' x 40' puddle on the unprotected ground north of the GPUs field tested at 1875 mS conductance. I discussed this with Wes who arranged for the liquid to be removed.A 40 foot channel of water immediately east of the central outfall from the pad field tested at 2030 uS conductance. Liquid draining from the north center outfall into the basin field tested at 2020 uS conductance. Liquid in the sediment basin next to the northeast overflow field tested at 1380 uS conductance. Liquid was observed flowing through the northern most compost filter sock and leaving the site; the liquid field tested at 1201 uS conductance. Liquid flowing past the LOD field tested at 1409 uS conductance.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1200 hours.

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection

Comments: On 4/22/2026, a follow-up inspection to IR 4164849 was conducted, where violations were issued in response to reported sloughing at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. The sloughing was reportedly discovered by the operator on 3/20/2026, on the cutslope above the access road.An Individual Erosion and Sedimentation permit (ESP) was issued by the Department for this site on 1/26/2024 and expires on 1/25/2029.The following was observed during the inspection:The sloughing remains on the cutslope above the access road, as reported by the operator on 3/20/2026 (photos 19-21). This area appears to be unchanged since the time of 4164849 and does not appear to immediately threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. No pipeline markers and/or gas well equipment were observed below the slough. Temporary stabilization is applied to the slough. Repairs are reportedly expected to begin once the ground dries adequately to allow for machine operation.The former slope repair area north of the well pad has nearly established 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage (photos 12 and 13). However, temporary stabilization was observed on a small portion of the other former slope repair area south of the well pad (photos 14 and 15). The Department requests clarification from the operator regarding what occurred in this location and why temporary stabilization was applied. Please provide this clarification electronically to the Department no later than 5/01/2026. Violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of operator's response. The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 1 and 22). Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMP) appear to be constructed in the locations shown on the approved ESP plan drawings (photos 16-18).The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 23). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) inspection log, and ESP approval letter are on site (photos 2-6). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Seven gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production (photo 11). Well 6H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photo 24). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection (photo 7). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units on site are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 9 and 10). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4164849 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) on 7/14/2025 at 0630 hours. The weather ranged from mid-70s to mid-80s degrees throughout the day. The inspection was conducted in response to a report of a well control incident occurring on the 7H well which resulted in a release of produced fluids. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #390569 is tied to the release in CTS.According to Repsol, at ~1830 hours on 7/13/2025 a pressure issue on the 7H well caused the uncontrolled release of produced fluid up the casing[s] to the pad surface. Efforts to control pressure and prevent the escaping fluids have failed so far. Secondary containments were overtopped and fluid has and continues to escape the pad surface. A temporary berm was constructed along the northwestern edge around the western corner of the pad, below the fill slope, to collect fluids (photos #3 to 5). The "corner" berm below the fill slope was said to be completed around 0000 hours on 7/14/2025. Numerous gravel berms were constructed on the pad surface to help prevent fluids from escaping the pad surface but are failing in numerous spots. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed sheet flowing from numerous areas along the southwestern edge of the pad (see photo #8 for example). Fluid observed in the western corner of the stormwater control basin was field measured for electrical conductivity and returned a reading of >19.99mS/cm. ~1000 hours: A Repsol representative onsite indicated that larger pumps were en route to catch up on fluid collection that is being pooled on the western corner of the well pad (photo #9). According to Repsol, the pumps being brought in should be able to catch up on the fluid that is pooled on the surface.A secondary berm/trench was constructed below the first "corner" berm below the fill slope sometime throughout the day. A break in the first berm was dug to allow fluid collected to flow into the secondary berm. The secondary berm is flowing fluid into the stormwater control basin onsite (see photos #10-12).Fluid was able to reach the stormwater control basin shown in photo #7. The DEP collected a sample for standard analysis code 942 from the basin which was field measured at >19.99mS/cm (Sample #0983-510).A third (tertiary) berm/trench was later constructed below the secondary berm and was built into the stormwater control basin. The short side wall of the basin was removed to allow for excess fluid build-up in the basin to collect in the third berm. The secondary and tertiary berms are utilized to relieve hydrostatic pressure from the "corner" berm. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed on the pad surface, in the constructed berms, in the pad's stormwater channels and in the stormwater control basin. Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were observed directly down-gradient of the well pad, below the constructed "corner" berm and along the installed surface waterline. Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were also observed along the surface waterline in the field adjacent to the pad (photo #13).Repsol identified and initiated the screening and sampling of nearby water supplies as required by 25 Pa. Code 78a.66b(4).Based on the findings of this inspection report, violations of the following are cited against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, SWMA 301 and Clean Streams Law 401. A violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.55(f) is cited against API #015-23892 as immediately corrected.I departed the well pad at 1430 hours.

Comments: Inspection completed in response to a notification received from the operator on October 2, 2019 of a release discovered on the same day. The operator stated in the notification that they believe that a can containing secondary containment leaked produced water onto compromised secondary containment which caused a release to the pad surface. The operator estimated the volume of release at 2 barrels. DEP Compliance Specialist Chris Southard accompanied me on this inspection. This area did have electrical conductivity readings which were elevated comapred to the rest of the pad. We walked the site with Mr. Deming. We walked around the infiltration basin to the south of the pad as well but could not find any water in the basin, nor in the rock-lined ditch which leads to the basin, to screen. Due to the estimated volume of the release, the Department recommends pursing Act 2. Violations noted.

Comments: On 02/19/2026, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the SPESAK F41 in Fallowfield Township, Washington County. The following was observed during inspection:-The Department found a release and spill of over range fluid leaking from a cracked hose to production tank labeled #1. I observed discolored elevated fluid of 5.89 mS/cm and 6.89 mS/cm throughout the Earthen Berm contaiment. It appears the spill is greater than 42 gallons and the Department recommends following Act 2 remediation guidelines. No rainwater outlet was observed (Photo 1-7).-An unnamed stream was 147 ft downslope of the release. I observed no elevated fluid within stream at the time of inspection (Photo 8 and 9).-Field Scout Conductivity probe was calibrated on 02/18/2026.-The Department contacted Diversified Lisa Raffle at the time of observation. I was contacted by Glen at Diversified stating a well tender was going to come shut-in the well and a truck to remove the fluid as soon as possible. Violations are being issued for: 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), 78.66(b).
